audit.whatIsWrong: Every warning about Mega Gnar points at GNAR! as an 'AoE stun'. It is not one on its own — it only stuns if it throws you into terrain — and Wallop, the ability that does stun outright, is never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot's GNAR! text: he 'throws everything around him in a chosen direction, dealing damage and slowing them. Any enemy that hits a wall is stunned and takes bonus damage.' Riot's Wallop (Mega W): he can 'rear up on his hind legs and smash down on the area in front of him, stunning enemies in an area' — on 7 seconds. So the 90s ultimate is a displacement you can position against by standing away from walls, and the every-7-second stun is the one that actually cuts your Aegis Assault channel.
audit.corrected: Fight Mega Gnar in open lane so GNAR! has no wall to stun you against; the CC to respect on cooldown is Wallop's 7s.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Hyper hops' merges two different abilities, and Boomerang Throw's range is never given against yours.
audit.why: Hyper is the mini-form W — a passive hype on his attacks and spells — while Hop is the E leap that bounces off units to travel further, on 22/19.5/17/14.5/12. Boomerang Throw is 1100 range on 16s at rank 1, and catching it reduces that cooldown. Against Comet Spear's 575 and Shield Vault's 600, 1100 is the whole spacing problem, and Hop at 22s is the longest escape cooldown in the lane.
audit.corrected: Hop and Hyper separated; 1100 against 575 stated, and Hop's 22s named as the window to punish.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, so 'watch his rage bar' is the only timing instruction on the page.
audit.why: Boomerang Throw 16s at rank 1 and reduced on catch, Hop 22s, Wallop 7s, GNAR! 90/60/30. Rage is not on a cooldown at all, which is exactly why the numbers that ARE on cooldowns — Hop's 22s and Wallop's 7s — are what you plan around.
audit.corrected: Real numbers into the spikes, wants, early, mid, cooldown block and interactions row.

audit.why: 52.16% over 903 games with the chart giving Pantheon levels 3-5 and both item stages against Gnar's level 1 and level 6. Coverage flagged this chart as contradicting the win rate, but on disk it reads Pantheon 3 stages to Gnar 2 — that is consistent with a 52% lane, so the flag looks stale.

edits.before: Level 1 you are king — your point-and-click W stun plus a Q tap is the strongest opener here, so look for that trade before mini-Gnar finds boomerang spacing. But the moment he has range, he kites: do not chase his hops across the wave, and respect that a returning Boomerang Throw (Q) double-dips on you. Your E directional block can eat a boomerang if you channel into it, but you cannot pin him down for a kill the way you can an immobile melee.
edits.after: Level 1 you are king — Shield Vault's leap-stun plus a Q tap is the strongest opener here, so take the trade before Boomerang Throw's 1100 range exists. Once it does he kites: don't chase Hop across the wave, and respect that the boomerang damages going out AND coming back, with the catch cutting its 16s. Facing it lets Aegis Assault eat it, but you still cannot pin him the way you pin an immobile melee.

edits.before: This is where the lane slips. Mini-Gnar out-spaces your Q and your W is your only gap-close — if you whiff it, you eat free poke. Watch his rage bar like a hawk: when it fills, your W all-in walks straight into mega-Gnar's GNAR! (R) AoE stun and a wall, flipping the trade hard. At 6 your answer is not the 1v1 — it's Grand Starfall (R) roaming to mid or a gank to turn your early tempo into kills somewhere Gnar can't kite.
edits.after: This is where the lane slips. Boomerang Throw reaches 1100 against your 575, and Shield Vault is your only way in — whiff it and you eat free poke for 13 seconds. Watch the Rage bar: at full, Wallop stuns on 7s and cuts any Aegis Assault, while GNAR! only stuns you if it throws you into terrain, so hold the open half of the lane. At 6 the answer is a Grand Starfall roam, not the duel.

edits.after: At level 1 Shield Vault's leap-stun plus a Q tap is one of the strongest openers in the game, and Boomerang Throw's 1100 range is not ranked yet.

notes: The page's central warning was wrong in a way that changes where you stand: GNAR! is not an AoE stun, it is a displacement that stuns ONLY if it throws you into terrain, so the counterplay is holding the open half of the lane rather than avoiding Mega form altogether. Meanwhile Wallop — the Mega W that genuinely stuns in an area on a 7-second cooldown, and therefore the ability that actually cancels an Aegis Assault channel — was not mentioned anywhere in either layer. Coverage also flagged 'level chart contradicts data' for this matchup; on disk the chart gives Pantheon three stages to Gnar's two, which fits 52.16%, so that flag appears to be stale rather than a real defect.
